reasons: The principle of a replacement building in the countryside is considered acceptable because it would be a like-for-like replacement of a former barn on the same footprint, used for winter hay storage for equestrian livestock on associated land and vehicle storage associated with the applicant’s small-scale rural enterprise. Its size, scale and rural-related use are considered appropriate in this location, subject to restricting the use, and the proposal accords with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 25 Part 4 and NPPF paragraphs 88 and 89.

The replacement barn would have a simple rectangular form, timber cladding and agricultural roof profile, and would sit within a landscape bordered by mature trees, so it would retain a rural agricultural appearance and would not harm the character of the countryside, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 25 and 41.

The site is within Flood Zone 3, but the Environment Agency raised no objection subject to compliance with the submitted Flood Risk Assessment. A sequential test was not required for this like-for-like replacement, which would not include residential or office accommodation or attract public visits, and the building would remain on the original footprint with the same surface water disposal provision. The proposal is therefore acceptable in flood risk terms, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 57 and NPPF Section 14.

The nearest dwelling, associated with the kennels to the north-east, is approximately 80 metres away, and the development would be sufficiently distant not to cause unacceptable harm to neighbouring living conditions, subject to construction management controls.

The amended layout provides sufficient turning space in front of the building, and surfacing/hardstanding controls would prevent mud and debris being carried onto the carriageway. The proposal would therefore protect highway safety, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 13(A).
conditions: The development must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission. Reason: Condition required to be imposed by Section 91 (as amended) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

The development must be carried out and completed entirely in accordance with the terms of this permission and the approved plan: Proposed Plans and Elevations CWX-PEAT-2025-100B. Reason: To ensure that the development is carried out in accordance with the application as approved.

Before the development is brought into use, that part of the site to be used by vehicles shall be surfaced, drained and, where necessary, marked out in a manner to be approved in writing by the local planning authority. Reason: To ensure highway safety is protected in accordance with Policy 13(A) of the Doncaster Local Plan.

No development shall take place, including any works of demolition, until a Construction Method Statement has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The approved statement shall be adhered to throughout the construction period and shall provide for: parking of site operatives’ and visitors’ vehicles; loading and unloading of plant and materials; storage of plant and materials; erection and maintenance of security hoarding, including decorative displays and facilities for public viewing where appropriate; wheel washing facilities; measures to control noise and the emission of dust and dirt during construction; and recycling/disposal of waste resulting from demolition and construction works. Reason: To safeguard the living conditions of neighbouring residents and in the interests of highway safety.

Before any construction works are started, a Construction Impact Management Plan indicating measures to mitigate the effects of construction activity and associated vehicle movements upon neighbouring living conditions and highway safety shall be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority. The mitigation measures shall include limitation of noise, means of enclosure of the construction sites, any proposed external security lighting, control of dust emissions, control of deposition of mud or debris on the highway, and routing of contractors’ vehicles. The approved measures shall be carried out at all times during construction. Reason: To safeguard the living conditions of neighbouring residents.

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the submitted flood risk assessment by EWE Associates Ltd, reference 2024/3111 Final Report RevB dated 9 September 2025, including the following mitigation measures: finished floor levels shall be set no lower than 5.90 metres above Ordnance Datum as detailed in Section 5 of the FRA; flood resilience and resistance measures shall be installed to a level of 500mm above finished ground floor levels; and flooding will not be increased off-site. These measures shall be fully implemented prior to occupation, subsequently in accordance with the scheme’s timing/phasing arrangements, and retained and maintained thereafter throughout the lifetime of the development. Reasons: To reduce the risk of flooding to the proposed development and future occupants, and to prevent flooding elsewhere.

Notwithstanding the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 or the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 1995 (as amended), the use of the site shall be for no purpose other than the storage of vehicles and/or storage of equestrian equipment, accessories and feed. There shall be no commercial trade of goods or services on the site. Reason: To restrict uses to those proposed by the applicant, as the site is not in a sustainable location for a commercial enterprise.
